description: Core LocalRAG Q/A fixture covering in-scope and out-of-scope questions about the project itself.

records.question: What is LocalRAG?
records.reference_answer: LocalRAG is an offline-first Retrieval-Augmented Generation system that keeps documents, models, and computation entirely on the local machine.

citations.text: LocalRAG is an offline-first RAG system. Your documents, your models, your machine.
It uses Chroma as the vector store and Ollama for embeddings and LLM inference.

records.question: Which vector store does LocalRAG use?
records.reference_answer: LocalRAG uses ChromaDB as its vector store for persisting and retrieving document embeddings.

citations.text: LocalRAG stores all document embeddings in ChromaDB, a persistent on-disk vector database.
The Chroma collection name and persist path are configurable via environment variables.

records.question: What embedding model is used by default?
records.reference_answer: The default embedding model is nomic-embed-text, which is run locally via Ollama.

citations.text: The default embedding model is nomic-embed-text. It is pulled and served by Ollama.
You can override the embedding model with the OLLAMA_EMBED_MODEL environment variable.

records.question: How do I ingest a PDF file?
records.reference_answer: You can ingest a PDF file using the POST /ingest endpoint with the file path, or with the localrag ingest CLI command.

citations.text: Use POST /ingest with a JSON body containing the path field pointing to the PDF file.
The CLI command `localrag ingest /path/to/file.pdf` also ingests a single file.

records.question: What LLM is used by default for answering questions?
records.reference_answer: The default LLM is llama3.2, served locally via Ollama.

citations.text: By default LocalRAG uses llama3.2 for the chat/completion step.
The LLM model tag is configurable via OLLAMA_LLM_MODEL.

records.question: How do I run the LocalRAG API server?
records.reference_answer: Run the API server with `uv run uvicorn localrag.api.main:app` or via Docker Compose.

citations.text: Start the API with: uv run uvicorn localrag.api.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
Alternatively use docker compose up to start all services including the API.

records.question: What is the chunk size used during ingestion?
records.reference_answer: The default chunk size is 512 characters with a 50-character overlap between adjacent chunks.

citations.text: Text is split into chunks of up to CHUNK_CHARS characters (default 512).
Adjacent chunks share CHUNK_OVERLAP_CHARS characters (default 50) to preserve context at boundaries.

records.question: Can I restrict which directories are allowed for ingestion?
records.reference_answer: Yes, setting INGEST_ROOTS to a list of allowed paths restricts ingestion to those directories only.

citations.text: INGEST_ROOTS limits the HTTP ingest API to files under the specified root directories.
An empty INGEST_ROOTS list (default) disables path restriction and allows any accessible file.

records.question: What authentication mechanism does the API use?
records.reference_answer: The API uses an X-API-Key header for authentication, configured via the API_KEY environment variable. It is disabled when API_KEY is empty.

citations.text: Set API_KEY in .env to enable API key authentication via the X-API-Key request header.
When API_KEY is empty (the default), authentication is disabled and all requests are accepted.

records.question: How do I switch from Ollama to OpenAI?
records.reference_answer: Set LLM_BACKEND=openai and provide your OpenAI API key in OPENAI_API_KEY.

citations.text: Change LLM_BACKEND to openai and set OPENAI_API_KEY to your OpenAI secret key.
OPENAI_MODEL controls which OpenAI model is used (default: gpt-4o-mini).

records.question: What Prometheus metrics does LocalRAG expose?
records.reference_answer: LocalRAG exposes localrag_query_duration_seconds, localrag_tokens_used_total, localrag_chunks_retrieved_total, and localrag_ingested_documents_total at the /metrics endpoint.

citations.text: The /metrics endpoint exposes localrag_query_duration_seconds (histogram) and localrag_tokens_used_total (counter).
localrag_chunks_retrieved_total and localrag_ingested_documents_total track retrieval and ingestion activity.

records.question: What file formats can LocalRAG ingest?
records.reference_answer: LocalRAG supports PDF, DOCX, Markdown, plain text, and source code files.

citations.text: Supported parsers: PDF (pypdf), DOCX (python-docx), Markdown, plain text, and source code files.
The loader dispatches each file to the appropriate parser based on file extension.

records.question: Where is configuration stored?
records.reference_answer: Configuration is loaded from environment variables and an optional .env file via pydantic-settings.

citations.text: All configuration is managed by the Settings class using pydantic-settings.
Settings are read from the process environment and optionally from a .env file in the working directory.

records.question: How can I see available CLI commands?
records.reference_answer: Run `localrag --help` to see all available commands, or `localrag <command> --help` for command-specific help.

citations.text: Use `localrag --help` for a list of commands.
Each sub-command also supports `--help` for detailed usage.

records.question: What is the health check endpoint?
records.reference_answer: GET /health returns the API status, whether Ollama is reachable, the Chroma persist path, and the list of collections.

citations.text: GET /health checks Ollama connectivity and returns status, ollama_ok, chroma_path, and collections.
The health endpoint does not require API key authentication.

records.question: How is context built for the LLM prompt?
records.reference_answer: The retriever fetches the top-k most similar document chunks, which are assembled into a prompt using a system message and the retrieved context.

citations.text: The retriever embeds the question and retrieves the top RAG_TOP_K chunks from ChromaDB.
build_prompt assembles the system message, retrieved chunks, and question into the final prompt.

records.question: Does LocalRAG support streaming responses?
records.reference_answer: Yes, POST /query/stream streams answer tokens via Server-Sent Events (SSE).

citations.text: POST /query/stream returns tokens incrementally as Server-Sent Events.
Each token event carries the token text; a final event includes source references.

records.question: What is the capital of Mars?
records.reference_answer: I don't know. Mars has no capital city; it is not inhabited.

citations.text: LocalRAG is an offline-first RAG system for local document retrieval.
It uses Chroma and Ollama for vector storage and language model inference.

records.question: What is the cost of using Ollama models?
records.reference_answer: Ollama models run locally and are free; there is no per-token cost.

citations.text: Ollama models are served locally and have zero API cost.
Cloud providers such as OpenAI and Anthropic have per-token pricing; Ollama does not.

records.question: Can I rebuild the vector store collection?
records.reference_answer: Yes, POST /collections/rebuild or `localrag collections rebuild` drops and re-ingests all stored sources.

citations.text: POST /collections/rebuild re-embeds all previously ingested sources from scratch.
Sources that no longer exist on disk are removed from the collection automatically.

records.question: How do I fix ERR_LOCALRAG_42?
records.reference_answer: Fix ERR_LOCALRAG_42 by deleting the stale cache directory and restarting the service.

citations.text: Troubleshooting: ERR_LOCALRAG_42 indicates stale cache metadata. Delete ./data/cache and restart.
General startup issues can also come from missing model pulls.
